title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper addresses unsupervised anomaly detection on data with varying local densities, where distance- and density-based methods either miss local anomalies or require costly parameter tuning. It proposes SVEAD, which builds an ensemble of random Voronoi partitions by sampling anchors and scores points by normalized within-cell distance weighted by cell mean distance. Experiments on 45 ADBench datasets report SVEAD mean AUC-ROC 0.8538 and AUC-PR 0.5000, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio.

match_target.why: User hint specifies Table 4, SVEAD AUC-ROC on cardio; cardio is small (1831 samples) and cheap, while still exercising the ensemble Voronoi scoring mechanism on a real-world medical anomaly dataset.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: Table 5 reports SVEAD AUC-ROC standard deviation 0.0063 for cardio over 5 runs; 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189, rounded to the paper's 4-decimal precision.

requirements.stmt: The detector must produce an anomaly score that is higher for anomalies than for normal instances.
requirements.quote: assigns higher scores to anomalous instances and lower scores to normal instances

requirements.stmt: Evaluation must be unsupervised in prediction: labels are used only after scores are produced.
requirements.quote: the labels are used to compute the AUC-ROC and AUC-PR for each dataset only after the models have made predictions

requirements.stmt: SVEAD must construct an ensemble of random Voronoi-style space partitions.
requirements.quote: constructs an ensemble of random space partitions via Voronoi diagram

requirements.stmt: For each partition, anchors must be sampled from the dataset without replacement.
requirements.quote: m points from the dataset X without replacement

requirements.stmt: Each data point must be assigned to its nearest anchor under Euclidean distance.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈ X is assigned to its nearest anchor

requirements.stmt: Within-cell scoring must use the normalized distance δ/δmax.
requirements.quote: the first term δ/δmax normalizes the distance by the maximum cell radius

requirements.stmt: Within-cell scoring must multiply by the cell mean distance δmean.
requirements.quote: the second term δmean represents the mean distance within the cell

requirements.stmt: If a cell contains only its anchor, that point's score must be skipped for that partition.
requirements.quote: we skip scoring for this point in this partition and rely on the other t − 1 partitions in the ensemble average

requirements.stmt: The final anomaly score must be the arithmetic mean across ensemble partitions.
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean

requirements.stmt: Performance must be measured with AUC-ROC and AUC-PR, averaged over 5 runs.
requirements.quote: We adopt Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and Area Under the Precision-Recall curve (AUC-PR)

requirements.stmt: SVEAD's anchor count m must be grid-searched over powers of two while ensemble size t is fixed at 100.
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100

requirements.stmt: The benchmark datasets must come from ADBench.
requirements.quote: We evaluate SVEAD on 45 publicly available benchmark datasets widely used in anomaly detection from ADBench

requirements.stmt: The implementation should preserve the paper's claimed linear scaling with n when m, t, and d are fixed or small.
requirements.quote: Since m ≪ n in practice, this scales linearly with dataset size.

data.name: cardio (ADBench)
data.how_to_get: Obtain the cardio dataset from the ADBench benchmark by Han et al., 2022; official repository: https://github.com/MLGroupJLU/ADBench. Use the provided cardio table with 1831 samples, 21 features, and 176 anomalies.

stated_compute: The test device is on CPU @AMD Ryzen 9 9950X and GPU @Nvidia RTX 4090.
